title: Best AirPlus Dehumidifier (2026): Max 26 to 70 Pint Compared
dek: AirPlus has quietly become one of Amazon’s busiest dehumidifier brands. Here’s which model fits your space — and how to read its pint ratings.
description: The best AirPlus dehumidifier for every room, from the Max 26 to the 70 pint, plus how AirPlus pint ratings compare, where to find the manual and quick fixes.
intro: If you’ve searched Amazon for a dehumidifier lately, you’ve almost certainly seen an **AirPlus dehumidifier** near the top of the results. The brand sells everything from compact bedroom units to tall 50- and 70-pint models sized for basements, often priced below the big appliance names, with drain hoses, timers and humidistats included.

The lineup is easy to like and a little harder to compare. AirPlus’s model names are similar, several units claim the same coverage, and the listings don’t always say which test their pint figures come from. Below, we sort the current AirPlus range by the room it actually suits, explain how to read the ratings, and cover the manual and troubleshooting questions owners ask most.
topPicksLead: For most homes, the **AirPlus Max 50 Pint Tall** is the AirPlus to buy: it’s sized for large rooms and basements, holds a set humidity with its built-in humidistat, and drains continuously through a hose.

products.name: AirPlus Max 50 Pint Tall Dehumidifier
pros: Sized for basements and large rooms
Built-in humidistat holds a set level
Continuous drainage through a hose
Mid-century retro styling looks at home upstairs
cons: Pint rating basis isn’t clearly stated
products.whyWeLoveIt: It’s the most versatile model in the lineup: big enough for a damp basement, but designed to look like furniture rather than an appliance, so it also works in a living room or primary suite.
products.performance: AirPlus sizes the Max 50 for up to 4,500 square feet and lists an intelligent humidistat, continuous drainage and a drain hose. Set it to 45–50% and connect the hose to a floor drain, and it will cycle on and off without bucket trips. As with any brand, judge it against the DOE rating rather than the coverage claim; our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) shows what each size really handles.

products.name: AirPlus 70 Pint Dehumidifier with Drain Hose (4,500 sq ft)
pros: Auto-defrost for cool basements
Four operating modes and a 24-hour timer
Dual protection system, per AirPlus
Drain hose included
cons: Same coverage claim as the Max 50
No pump, so it needs a drain below the outlet
products.whyWeLoveIt: Basements run cooler than living spaces, and that’s where auto-defrost matters: it keeps the coil from icing when the floor is chilly in spring. This is the AirPlus we’d put next to a floor drain and leave alone for the season.
products.performance: AirPlus rates it for up to 4,500 square feet and lists four operating modes, a 24-hour timer, auto-defrost and what it calls a dual protection system. The included drain hose lets it run continuously into a floor drain or sump. If your only drain is above the floor, a pump unit is the better buy — see our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

products.name: AirPlus Max 70 Pint Quiet Dehumidifier
pros: Quiet sleep mode for overnight running
Highest marketed capacity in the Max line
Drain hose for continuous use
cons: Big for a bedroom despite the sleep mode
Pint rating basis isn’t clearly stated
products.whyWeLoveIt: Open-plan homes and finished basements often double as living space, so a large unit that can dial itself down at night is worth having. The Max 70 pairs the line’s biggest headline capacity with a sleep mode.
products.performance: AirPlus sizes it for up to 4,500 square feet, the same as the Max 50 and the standard 70-pint, and lists a quiet sleep mode and drain hose. Since the coverage claims match, choose between them on features: sleep mode here, auto-defrost on the standard 70. Owners who sleep near their dehumidifier should also read our [best quiet dehumidifier](/best/best-quiet-dehumidifier/) picks.

products.name: AirPlus Max 30 Pint Tall Dehumidifier
pros: Sized for bedrooms and mid-size rooms
Quiet sleep mode
Drain hose for continuous use
Small enough for an RV or camper
cons: Not enough for a wet basement
Far less capacity than the Max 50
products.whyWeLoveIt: Most rooms that need a dehumidifier are bedrooms, offices and guest rooms, not basements. The Max 30 is the AirPlus sized for them, with a sleep mode so it can run overnight.
products.performance: AirPlus sizes it for up to 1,500 square feet and pitches it for bedrooms, large rooms and campers, with a quiet sleep mode and a drain hose. In practice, it’s a comfortable fit for a single damp room of a few hundred square feet. If you’re dehumidifying a camper, our [best RV dehumidifier](/best/best-rv-dehumidifier/) guide covers power and mounting.

products.name: AirPlus Max 26 Pint Small Dehumidifier
pros: Wheels for rolling between rooms
Auto-defrost and 24-hour timer
Continuous-drainage option
Three operating modes
products.whyWeLoveIt: The Max 26 is the AirPlus to move around: a laundry room on wash day, a bathroom after showers, a guest room before visitors arrive. Wheels and a compact body make that easy.
products.performance: AirPlus sizes it for up to 1,500 square feet and lists a 2.5-liter tank, continuous drainage, auto-defrost, a 24-hour timer and three modes. Like the Max 30, it’s best treated as a one-room machine. It’s also one of our picks for [500 sq ft spaces](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-500-sq-ft/).

products.name: Frigidaire 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Built-In Pump (FFAP5033W1)
pros: Built-in pump pushes water up to a sink or window

Pump, gravity hose or bucket drainage

products.whyWeLoveIt: None of the AirPlus models we can verify on Amazon has a built-in pump. If your basement drain is above floor level, this Frigidaire is the straightforward alternative, and its capacity is stated on the current DOE basis.
products.performance: It’s a 50-pint compressor unit under the 2019 DOE procedure with a digital humidistat. You can pump water up to a utility sink, drain it by gravity or use the bucket. It tops our [best 50-pint dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-50-pint-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

blocks.text: AirPlus also sells small thermoelectric minis for closets and bathrooms. Those remove ounces rather than pints a day; if that’s what you need, compare them in our [best mini dehumidifier](/best/best-mini-dehumidifier/) guide.

We don’t lab-test. For brand guides, we compare a maker’s current models on published specs, manuals, ENERGY STAR and DOE data where available, CPSC recall records and the patterns in owner reviews — what people praise and what fails. Every product here has a verified Amazon listing.

AirPlus listings emphasize coverage and features rather than test conditions, so we ranked its models by how well each suits a specific space, gave weight to humidistats, drainage and low-temperature operation, and added a DOE-rated pump alternative for basements that need lift.

sections.heading: What to look for in an AirPlus dehumidifier

items.label: Size by room, not coverage claim
items.text: Three AirPlus models claim 4,500 square feet. Use our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) and your dampness level instead.

items.label: Auto-defrost for basements
items.text: If the space drops below about 60°F, choose a model that lists auto-defrost, such as the 70 Pint or Max 26.

items.label: Sleep mode for living spaces
items.text: The Max 30 and Max 70 list a quiet sleep mode for overnight running.

items.label: A drain below the outlet
items.text: The AirPlus models here drain by gravity. Without a floor drain, sink or sump below the unit, you’ll be emptying the tank.

items.label: A separate hygrometer
items.text: Check the built-in reading against an independent [hygrometer](/best/best-hygrometer/) for the first few weeks.

blocks.text: Since 2019, the Department of Energy has rated dehumidifiers at 65°F, which cut every model’s official number: an old “70-pint” unit is about a 50-pint today. Some brands still headline older or hotter-test figures. AirPlus listings don’t always say which basis they use, and the fact that its 50- and 70-pint models claim identical coverage suggests the numbers aren’t directly comparable with DOE-rated models.
Before you buy, look up the exact model number in the ENERGY STAR product finder or check the rating label. If no DOE figure is listed, size conservatively and pick the larger model for a basement.

AirPlus units ship with a printed user manual, and many Amazon listings include a downloadable copy under the product documents section. Keep the model number from the rating label on the back handy when contacting AirPlus support.

items: **Not collecting water?** Check that the room is above about 41°F, the filter is clean and the humidistat is set below the room’s current reading.
**Full-tank light on with an empty tank?** Reseat the tank so its float moves freely.
**Hose not draining?** Make sure the hose runs downhill all the way, with no kinks or upward loops.
**Icing on the coil?** Let it defrost, raise the room temperature if you can, and clean the filter.
**Error code?** Unplug for 10 minutes, then check the manual’s code list before calling support.

blocks.text: Deeper fixes are in our [dehumidifier not working](/guides/dehumidifier-not-working/) and [dehumidifier maintenance](/guides/dehumidifier-maintenance/) guides.

AirPlus makes sensible, feature-rich dehumidifiers for the money. The **Max 50 Pint Tall** is the best all-rounder, the **70 Pint** suits cool basements thanks to auto-defrost, and the **Max 30** or **Max 26** cover single rooms. Size by your dampness rather than the coverage claims, and if you need a pump, step outside the brand to the **Frigidaire FFAP5033W1**. For other brands, see our [best dehumidifier brands](/best/best-dehumidifier-brands/) roundup.

faqs.a: They’re solid value picks with useful features such as humidistats, drain hoses, timers and, on some models, auto-defrost. The main caveat is that pint ratings aren’t always stated on the DOE basis, so size conservatively.

faqs.q: Where can I find the AirPlus dehumidifier manual?
faqs.a: A printed manual comes in the box, and many Amazon listings offer a downloadable copy in the product documents section. If you’ve lost both, contact AirPlus support with the model number from the rating label.

faqs.q: Which AirPlus dehumidifier should I buy?
faqs.a: For a basement or big open room, the Max 50 Pint Tall or the 70 Pint. For a bedroom or office, the Max 30. For a dehumidifier you’ll move between rooms, the Max 26 with wheels.

faqs.q: Does AirPlus make a dehumidifier with a pump?
faqs.a: None of the AirPlus models we could verify on Amazon has a built-in pump; they drain by tank or gravity hose. If you need lift, consider the Frigidaire FFAP5033W1.

faqs.q: How do I set up continuous drainage on an AirPlus dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Attach the included hose to the drain outlet, run it downhill to a floor drain, sump or sink, and make sure there are no kinks or upward bends. Many units need the tank in place for the hose outlet to work.

faqs.q: Is the AirPlus 70 pint dehumidifier really 70 pints?
faqs.a: AirPlus markets it as 70 pints, but it claims the same 4,500 sq ft as its 50-pint model, which suggests the figure isn’t on the current DOE basis. Check the ENERGY STAR finder or rating label for a DOE number.
